newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian peso, edging lower, ends at 995.
newsitem.headline: Colombian peso, edging lower, ends at 995.

text.p: Colombia's peso closed slightly lower, at 995 to the dollar, after the central bank threatened to intervene in the country's interbank market to curb the local currency's recent gains.

The central bank, or Banco de la Republica, flashed a message across electronic trading screens saying it intended to jump into the market and buy dollars at 990.40 if the peso reached that level later in the trading week, dealers said.
They said the warning, which came late in the session, established firm resistance for the peso at 990 and erased the currency's gains in early trading.
Dealers reported 372 trades for a total of $160 million and said the peso held in a range of 994.50 to 997.

The central bank has come under strong pressure to devalue the peso, or intervene aggressively in the interbank market to drive it lower, as the currency's sharp gains since June have cut the real value of exports and made Colombian goods less attractive in the global marketplace.
